questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: In Young's double-slit experiment, λ = 600 nm, the screen distance D = 1.0 m and the slit separation d = 0.5 mm. What is the fringe width?
questions.explanation: Fringe width is β = λD/d. Substituting gives β = (600 × 10⁻⁹ × 1.0)/(0.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m = 1.2 mm. Doubling the slit separation would halve the fringe width.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 10 Wave Optics, Sec 10.5 (Young's double-slit experiment)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: According to Huygens' principle, how is the new position of a wavefront obtained from its previous position?

options.text: By joining the source to the point of observation with a straight line
As the envelope of secondary wavelets drawn from every point of the previous wavefront
As the surface on which all rays meet at a single focus
As the locus of points where the path difference between two slits is zero

questions.explanation: Each point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets that spread out with the speed of the wave in the medium. The new wavefront is the forward envelope (common tangent surface) of these wavelets after a time t. This construction explains reflection and refraction of plane wavefronts.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 10 Wave Optics, Sec 10.2 (Huygens' principle)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: Sound from a room is heard clearly around a corner, but light from a lamp casts a sharp shadow behind the same corner. The best explanation is that:

options.text: Light is a transverse wave while sound is longitudinal, so light cannot bend around corners
Sound travels much faster than light in air
Sound wavelengths are comparable to the size of doorways and walls, whereas light wavelengths are far smaller
Light has a much higher frequency than sound, so it is absorbed at the corner

questions.explanation: Diffraction is significant when the size of an aperture or obstacle is comparable to the wavelength. Audible sound has wavelengths of roughly 1 cm to 20 m, comparable to doorways and walls, so it bends noticeably. Visible light, at about 400 to 700 nm, is far smaller, so its bending is usually too small to notice.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 10 Wave Optics, Sec 10.6 (Diffraction)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: Two coherent light sources produce an interference pattern. Their individual intensities are in the ratio 4 : 1. What is the ratio of the maximum to the minimum intensity in the pattern?
questions.explanation: Intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, so the amplitudes are in the ratio 2 : 1. Taking a1 = 2 and a2 = 1, the maximum intensity is proportional to (a1 + a2)² = 9 and the minimum to (a1 − a2)² = 1. The ratio is therefore 9 : 1.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 10 Wave Optics, Sec 10.4 to 10.5 (coherent sources and interference intensity)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: In a single-slit diffraction experiment, the slit width is 0.3 mm, the wavelength is 600 nm and the screen is 1.5 m away. What is the distance of the first dark fringe from the centre of the central maximum?
questions.explanation: For single-slit diffraction the first minimum satisfies a sinθ = λ, and for small angles the fringe position is y = Dθ = λD/a. Here y = (600 × 10⁻⁹ × 1.5)/(0.3 × 10⁻³) = 3 × 10⁻³ m = 3 mm. The full width of the central maximum is twice this value.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 10 Wave Optics, Sec 10.6 (Diffraction due to a single slit)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem:
Assertion: At the polarising angle, the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other.
Reason: At the polarising angle, tan i_p equals the refractive index of the medium.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: At the polarising angle i_p, Brewster’s law gives tan i_p = μ. Snell’s law then gives sin i_p / sin r = μ, so sin r = cos i_p and r = 90° − i_p. The reflected and refracted rays therefore make 90° with each other, so R explains A.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 10 Wave Optics, Sec 10.7 (Polarisation and Brewster's law)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: Unpolarised light of intensity I₀ passes through a polaroid (polariser) and then through a second polaroid (analyser) whose axis is at 60° to the first. What is the transmitted intensity?
questions.explanation: The first polaroid transmits half of the unpolarised intensity, giving I₀/2 of plane-polarised light. Malus’s law I = I₁cos²θ then gives (I₀/2)cos²60° = (I₀/2)(1/4) = I₀/8. Omitting the halving at the first polaroid gives the trap answer I₀/4.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 10 Wave Optics, Sec 10.7 (Polarisation and Malus's law)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: Two coherent sources each produce an intensity I₀ at a point on a screen. At a point where the path difference is λ/3, what is the resultant intensity?
questions.explanation: The resultant intensity is I = 4I₀cos²(φ/2), where φ = 2π × (path difference)/λ. For a path difference of λ/3, φ = 2π/3 and cos²(π/3) = 1/4, so I = 4I₀ × 1/4 = I₀. The maximum possible value is 4I₀, reached at zero path difference.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 10 Wave Optics, Sec 10.5 (Interference of light waves and Young’s experiment)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: In a Young's double-slit experiment with λ = 500 nm, D = 1 m and d = 1 mm, a thin transparent sheet of thickness 10 μm and refractive index 1.5 is placed in front of one slit. By how many fringes does the pattern shift?
questions.explanation: The shift of the pattern is x = (μ − 1)tD/d = 0.5 × 10 μm × 1 m / 1 mm = 5 mm. The fringe width is β = λD/d = 0.5 mm, so the number of fringes shifted is x/β = (μ − 1)t/λ = 10.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 10 Wave Optics, Sec 10.5 (Young's double-slit experiment)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: Maxwell introduced displacement current to make Ampère’s law consistent for a capacitor being charged. Displacement current is associated with which quantity?

options.text: The rate of change of electric flux, ε₀ dΦE/dt
The flow of free electrons in the connecting wire
The steady magnetic field produced by a constant current
The rate of change of magnetic monopole density

questions.explanation: Displacement current I_d = ε₀ dΦE/dt is not a flow of charge. It is the changing electric field between capacitor plates, and it produces a magnetic field just as a conduction current does. This correction keeps Ampère’s law consistent with charge conservation.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.2 (Displacement current)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: Given μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A and ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C²/(N·m²), what is the speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum, from c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀)?
questions.explanation: μ₀ε₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² ≈ 1.11 × 10⁻¹⁷ s²/m². Taking the reciprocal square root gives c ≈ 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. The speed of light is therefore fixed by the electric and magnetic properties of vacuum.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.2 to 8.3 (Electromagnetic waves and their speed)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: Arrange the following electromagnetic waves in order of increasing wavelength, that is, shortest wavelength first: gamma rays, visible light, microwaves and radio waves.

options.text: Gamma rays → visible light → microwaves → radio waves
Visible light → gamma rays → radio waves → microwaves
Radio waves → microwaves → visible light → gamma rays
Gamma rays → microwaves → visible light → radio waves

questions.explanation: Wavelength decreases as frequency increases across the spectrum. Radio waves are the longest, then microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays are the shortest. So increasing wavelength runs gamma rays, visible light, microwaves, radio waves.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.5 (Electromagnetic spectrum)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: Match List I (electromagnetic wave) with List II (use). List I: (a) Infrared (b) Ultraviolet (c) X-rays (d) Microwaves. List II: (P) Sterilising water and killing bacteria (Q) Radiographs of bones (R) Thermal imaging and TV remote controls (S) Radar and satellite communication. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Infrared is used in thermal imaging and remote controls (R), ultraviolet sterilises water and kills bacteria (P), X-rays produce radiographs of bones (Q), and microwaves are used in radar and satellite communication (S). The correct pairing is a–R, b–P, c–Q, d–S.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.5 (Electromagnetic spectrum and uses)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: An electromagnetic wave travels in the −z direction in vacuum. At an instant, its magnetic field points along +x. Along which direction does its electric field point at that instant?
questions.explanation: In an electromagnetic wave E, B and the direction of propagation are mutually perpendicular, with propagation along E × B. With B along +x and propagation along −z, E must be along +y, since ŷ × x̂ = −ẑ. So the electric field points along +y at that instant.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.3 (Electromagnetic waves: transverse nature and E, B directions)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: A microwave of frequency 1.5 GHz travels in vacuum. What is its wavelength? (Take c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.)
questions.explanation: The wavelength in vacuum is λ = c/f = (3 × 10⁸)/(1.5 × 10⁹) = 0.2 m. All electromagnetic waves travel at c in vacuum, so wavelength and frequency are inversely related.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.5 (Electromagnetic spectrum)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: Both surfaces of a biconvex lens of refractive index 1.5 have radii of curvature of magnitude 20 cm. What is the focal length of the lens in air?
questions.explanation: The lens maker's formula is 1/f = (μ − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂). With R₁ = +20 cm and R₂ = −20 cm (Cartesian sign convention), 1/f = 0.5 × (1/20 + 1/20) = 1/20 cm⁻¹, so f = 20 cm. Taking R₂ as +20 cm gives an infinite focal length, a common sign slip.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 9 Ray Optics, Sec 9.5 (Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: An equilateral prism of refracting angle A = 60° is set at minimum deviation, where the angle of minimum deviation is δm = 30°. What is the refractive index of the prism material?
questions.explanation: At minimum deviation the refractive index is μ = sin((A + δm)/2) / sin(A/2) = sin 45° / sin 30° = 0.707 / 0.5 ≈ 1.41. The prism angle and the minimum deviation together fix the index, so the formula is applied directly.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 9 Ray Optics, Sec 9.6 (Refraction through a prism)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: What is the approximate critical angle for light travelling from glass (μ = 1.5) to air?
questions.explanation: The critical angle C satisfies sin C = μ_air/μ_glass = 1/1.5 = 2/3. Since sin 42° ≈ 0.67, C ≈ 42°. Light striking the interface at angles larger than C undergoes total internal reflection.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 9 Ray Optics, Sec 9.4 (Total internal reflection)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: An astronomical telescope in normal adjustment has an objective of focal length 120 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 4 cm. What is its magnifying power?
questions.explanation: In normal adjustment the magnifying power of an astronomical telescope is M = f_o/f_e = 120/4 = 30. The final image is at infinity, and the length of the telescope is then f_o + f_e.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 9 Ray Optics, Sec 9.7 (Optical instruments: telescope)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: A sinusoidal alternating current i = I₀ sin ωt flows in a circuit. What is the average value of the current over one half cycle, from t = 0 to t = T/2?
questions.explanation: Over a complete cycle the average of a sine function is zero, but over a half cycle it is not. The half-cycle average is (2/T) ∫₀^(T/2) I₀ sin ωt dt = 2I₀/π ≈ 0.637 I₀. I₀/√2 is the rms value, which is a different quantity.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Ch 7 Alternating Current, Sec 7.2 (AC voltage applied to a resistor)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: A 100 μF capacitor is connected to a 50 Hz AC supply. What is its capacitive reactance?
questions.explanation: Capacitive reactance is X_C = 1/(ωC), where ω = 2πf ≈ 314 rad/s. So X_C = 1/(314 × 100 × 10⁻⁶) ≈ 31.8 Ω. Reactance falls as frequency or capacitance increases, and an ideal capacitor dissipates no average power.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Ch 7 Alternating Current, Sec 7.4 (AC voltage applied to a capacitor)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: A series LCR circuit has R = 3 Ω, X_L = 8 Ω and X_C = 4 Ω. An rms current of 10 A flows in the circuit. What is the average power dissipated?
questions.explanation: The impedance is Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²) = √(9 + 16) = 5 Ω, so cos φ = R/Z = 0.6. The average power is P = I_rms²R = 100 × 3 = 300 W, which equals V_rms I_rms cos φ = 50 × 10 × 0.6. Reactive components do not dissipate average power.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Ch 7 Alternating Current, Sec 7.5 and 7.7 (LCR series circuit and power in AC circuits)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: A series LCR circuit has L = 2 mH and C = 50 μF. What is its resonant frequency?
questions.explanation: Resonance occurs when X_L = X_C, at f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)). Here LC = 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ s², so √(LC) = 3.16 × 10⁻⁴ s and f₀ ≈ 503 Hz. At resonance the impedance is minimum and the power factor is unity.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Ch 7 Alternating Current, Sec 7.5 (LCR series circuit and resonance)

questions.subject: physics
questions.stem: An ideal step-up transformer has turns ratio N_p : N_s = 1 : 20 and is connected to a 230 V supply. If the secondary delivers 0.5 A to its load, what is the current in the primary coil?
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, V_p I_p = V_s I_s. The secondary voltage is 4600 V, so 230 × I_p = 4600 × 0.5 and I_p = 10 A. A step-up transformer raises voltage and reduces current on the secondary side in the same proportion.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Ch 7 Alternating Current, Sec 7.9 (Transformers)
